title: Tool parameter guardrails and compatibility adaptor spec
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Define a pragmatic JSON-schema driven format and compatibility adapter for runtime function/tool calling that enables strict parameter validation, human-friendly error messages, graceful coercion, streaming-friendly partial validation, and a backward-compatibility layer for legacy client call signatures.

Goals: (1) Standardize on a compact, extensible JSON schema representation that runtime and SDKs can serialize/deserialize easily; (2) Specify validator behavior (coercion, defaults, required/optional rules, numeric range policies, enum canonicalization); (3) Define a minimal error taxonomy with stable codes and user-facing message templates; (4) Design a compatibility adaptor to map legacy call payloads to the new callSpec at runtime; (5) Describe runtime streaming semantics when parameter validation is delayed or happens incrementally; (6) Provide test matrices and migration steps for SDKs and third-party integrators.

Why this ticket: multiple customer bug reports and internal incidents surfaced inconsistent parameter errors across SDKs (JS vs Python) and confusing messages during streaming tool runs. We need a single source-of-truth for parameter contract semantics plus a safety-first compatibility path so we don't break large customers during rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published in Confluence with full callSpec grammar and examples
Runtime validator library implemented in runtime repo and feature-flagged
Node and Python SDKs updated to emit standardized error codes and to call the compatibility adaptor when legacy shape detected
Integration test harness covering coercion, missing/extra parameters, enum normalization, and streaming incremental validation with 85%+ coverage
Migration runbook created with canary rollout steps and telemetry dashboards defined

test_plan: Unit tests for validator coercion rules: string->int, numeric range clamping, iso8601 date parsing fallback
Fuzz tests for unexpected extra fields to ensure graceful warning vs hard reject paths
Streaming test: send partial argument map over stream and assert incremental validation emits 'partial-accept' event then final 'validated' or 'error'
Compatibility tests mapping older 'params' arrays and positional args to named callSpec parameters
Cross-language parity: run same test matrix against Node and Python SDKs to confirm identical error codes/messages

2026-03-02 Design review: prefer explicit opt-in for aggressive coercion. Decision: default mode is strict, add 'compatibility_mode' flag in callSpec for permissive coercion per-call.

notes: CallSpec DSL: intentionally minimal. Example grammar (string inside ticket to avoid nested JSON): callSpec = { 'name': string, 'params': [{ 'id': string, 'type': 'string|int|float|bool|object|array|enum|date', 'required': bool, 'default': optional string, 'coerce': 'none|parse|relax', 'aliases': optional [string], 'doc': string }] , 'compatibility_mode': 'strict|permissive' }

Validator behaviour: 1) Validate presence of required params. 2) Apply aliases mapping (first match). 3) If coerce != 'none' attempt safe coercions: numeric parsing, boolean words, ISO date parse. 4) If coercion fails and compatibility_mode == 'permissive' then emit warning code W_COERCION_FALLBACK and pass raw value; else fail with E_TYPE_MISMATCH.

Error taxonomy (stable codes): E_MISSING_PARAM, E_TYPE_MISMATCH, E_ENUM_MISMATCH, E_COERCION_FAILED, E_EXTRA_PARAM_STRICT, W_COERCION_FALLBACK, W_DEPRECATED_PARAM, E_STREAM_TRUNCATED. Each error must carry: code, param_id, example_fix (string), retriable: 'true'|'false'.

Compatibility adaptor rules: map positional arrays -> named params using modelled signature for the version in request metadata. If metadata absent, try best-effort mapping then return W_DEPRECATED_PARAM for unmapped values. Expose adaptor telemetry: mapping_confidence (0-1), mapped_count, unmapped_keys.

Streaming notes: for large/streamed parameter blobs (e.g., multi-part objects or file refs) runtime will perform shallow validation on initial frame and schedule deep validation as data arrives. Validation events emitted over stream: 'validation_hint', 'validation_ok', 'validation_error'. SDKs should surface these to callers when available.

Migration playbook: 1) Feature-flagged rollout to 10% runtime capacity for 2 weeks, 2) Monitor E_* error rates and W_* warning trends, 3) Gradually increase to 50% with SDK updates, 4) Deprecate permissive compatibility after 90 days and inform customers with >5 W_DEPRECATED_PARAM warnings.
